steps: This flow is about hooks. Your code registers two of them: a pre tool use hook matched to Bash, and a post tool use hook with no matcher at all.
Asked to clean the build folder, Claude reaches for r m dash r f and emits a Bash tool use.
The pre tool use hook fires before permissions. Its block dangerous check sees r m dash r f and returns deny, so the command never runs.
The error tells Claude why it was blocked, so it picks a safe alternative and asks to list the build folder instead.
There is no r m dash r f this time, so the hook returns an empty object, meaning no objection. The gate runs the listing, and Bash shows the app binary and main object file.
Now the post tool use hook fires, but only for the call that actually ran. One audit line is written, and none for the blocked command.
Finally, the result reaches Claude, which answers that the build folder was inspected safely. Hooks blocked the danger and audited the rest.
